## TL;DR

**{{APP_NAME}}** is a Windows desktop app generated by
[AppHost](https://github.com/SeanShaffer88/AppHost). It starts life
with the boring parts already wired and tested: single-instance,
system tray, persistent settings, structured logging, crash capture,
background jobs with progress, supervised child processes, and an
update check that stays off until you configure it.

```sh
cargo test              # wiring tests (any host)
cargo build --release   # Windows: the real GUI app
```

## What you get out of the box

- **Window + tray** — a dark window (near-black, red accent) with a
  status line, and a tray icon. Right-click the tray icon (or use
  the window) for: Open, Run demo job, Run demo child process,
  Check for updates, Exit. Minimizing hides the window to the tray.
- **Single instance** — a second launch wakes the first window and
  exits, via the `Local\{{APP_ID}}-SingleInstance` mutex.
- **Settings** — `%APPDATA%\{{APP_ID}}\settings.json`, managed by
  SettingsKit: window position and a per-launch counter persist.
- **Logging** — `%APPDATA%\{{APP_ID}}\app.log` in LogKit's house
  format, including a startup line with the app name, version,
  `already_running` flag, and settings path.
- **Crash capture** — CrashKit writes a minidump + JSON sidecar to
  `%APPDATA%\{{APP_ID}}\crashes\` if the process crashes.
- **Demo job** — a three-step JobKit job (~2 s) reporting percent
  and ETA into the status line.
- **Demo child** — ProcessKit runs `cmd /C echo` with captured
  output, logged through LogKit.
- **Update check** — inert until you set `updates.manifest_url` in
  settings; empty means disabled (and the log says so). Nothing
  phones home by default.

The wiring is covered by integration tests (`tests/wiring.rs`) that
run the real kits — no mocks. The GUI itself is build-verified in
CI; its runtime behaviour on a real desktop is yours to verify on
first run.

## Layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `src/main.rs` | Thin binary: Windows GUI (window + tray in the wndproc) / headless self-check elsewhere |
| `src/lib.rs` | Library root, app identity constants, self-check |
| `src/platform.rs` | Data-directory resolution (Known Folder API on Windows) |
| `src/wiring/settings.rs` | SettingsKit adapter |
| `src/wiring/logging.rs` | LogKit adapter |
| `src/wiring/crash.rs` | CrashKit adapter |
| `src/wiring/jobs.rs` | JobKit demo job |
| `src/wiring/proc.rs` | ProcessKit demo child |
| `src/wiring/updates.rs` | UpdateKit check (disabled by default) |
| `tests/wiring.rs` | End-to-end wiring tests through the real kits |

Kit dependencies are pinned to exact revisions in `Cargo.toml`.
Bump one at a time, run the full gate, and re-check the kit's
`AGENTS.md` for contract changes before committing.

## Make it yours

- **Name / id** — regenerate with `scaffold-app.py --name ... --id ...`,
  or edit `APP_NAME` / `APP_ID` in `src/lib.rs`, the package name in
  `Cargo.toml`, the mutex/data-folder strings derive from `APP_ID`.
- **Icon** — the skeleton uses the stock Windows application icon.
  Add a real `.ico`, reference it from `app.rc`, and pass it to
  `LoadIconW` / the tray data instead of `IDI_APPLICATION`.
- **Manifest identity** — `app.manifest` names
  `SeanShaffer88.{{APP_ID}}`; change the publisher prefix if needed.
- **Settings** — add keys in `src/wiring/settings.rs` (dotted paths,
  e.g. `ui.theme`); defaults live in `AppSettings::default()` and
  are never written to disk by reads.
- **Update manifest** — set `updates.manifest_url` in
  `%APPDATA%\{{APP_ID}}\settings.json` to your UpdateKit manifest
  URL to enable checks. The check only fetches + evaluates the
  manifest; downloading/installing is your code to add.

## Verification status

- Wiring logic: **Verified** by `cargo test` (host + Windows CI).
- Windows GUI compile + link: **Verified** in CI
  (`cargo build --release` on windows-latest).
- GUI runtime (tray menu, single-instance wake, window restore on a
  real desktop): **Unverified** until run on a real Windows machine.
